subject: Forensic log packaging: filtered exports, custody notes, and delivery timeline
messages:
From: Daniel Park <dpark@acmehealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: security@acmehealth.com
Date: 2026-04-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: scoped admin activity extract and custody notes for SIG/SOC2 review

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for taking this. As part of our SIG and SOC2 evidence collection we need a scoped extract of admin activity and operator logs covering 2025-10-01 through 2026-03-31. Specifically we need:  
- All admin-level actions (role changes, privilege grants/revokes, key rotations, console login events)
- Associated context: timestamp (UTC), actor (internal id and email), target resource id, IP, user agent, session id, and any request payload references (if available)
- Proof of custody: export manifest, SHA256 checksums, and delivery URLs; description of who handled the export and when
- Retention/export formats: we prefer newline-delimited JSON (JSONL) or compressed CSV; indicate if PII is present and redaction strategy

Attached is a short questionnaire (acme_sg_questionnaire.xlsx) with the fields we are validating against the SIG checklist. Can you confirm:  
1) What exactly you will include in the extract schema?
2) Where the files will be staged and for how long (we need 30 days of availability minimum)?
3) Whether you can provide a signed manifest and checksums?

We'd like an ETA and any constraints (PII scrub, sampling for very high-volume events) so we can schedule the evidence handoff. I'm looping in our SecOps alias for legal review.

Thanks,
Daniel Park
Security Engineer
Acme Health

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <dpark@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, security@acmehealth.com
Date: 2026-04-19T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: scoped admin activity extract and custody notes for SIG/SOC2 review

Hi Daniel — thanks for the detail, this is clear and actionable. High level plan below; I can schedule a short handoff call if you want to go over the manifest format.

What we'll include (first-pass):
- Event fields: utc_timestamp, actor_email, actor_id, action_type, resource_id, resource_type, ip_address, user_agent, session_id, request_id, change_summary, prior_state_ref (when applicable)
- Operator/admin categories: console_admin, api_admin, key_admin, service_account_ops (we'll map to your SIG fields)
- Audit provenance: export_agent_version, export_run_id, exported_by (redwood operator), export_start/end_time

Formats and delivery:
- Primary export: JSONL (UTF-8), gzipped. Secondary: CSV (comma, RFC4180) on request.
- Staging: encrypted S3 bucket with KMS-managed keys (AWS KMS). We'll provide a presigned HTTPS URL (7 days) and a signed manifest file (signed with our internal artifact key) that includes file names, sizes, and SHA256 checksums.
- Retention: files remain in staging for 30 days by default. If you need longer, we can configure a 90/180 day window by request (charges apply).

PII / redaction:
- We will not include full request payloads by default. If a payload reference exists, we'll include a payload_ref id. For fields flagged as sensitive we can either redact values or provide tokenized/hashed values. Need your preference on redaction level.

Sampling and limits:
- For very high volume event types (console_telemetry), we propose deterministic sampling (1:100) unless you request full export; will note sampling rate in manifest.

Next steps / ETA:
- Karthik will draft the export spec and run a test extract for a 7-day slice by 2026-04-21.
- If that looks good, full window (6 months) export scheduled for 2026-04-23 and staged same day.

Attachments: export_spec_v1.pdf (high-level fields + manifest example)

Cheers,
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Exec — Security & Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

> Hi Jordan,
>
> Thanks for taking this. As part of our SIG and SOC2 evidence collection we need a scoped extract of admin activity and operator logs covering 2025-10-01 through 2026-03-31....

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Daniel Park <dpark@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-20T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: scoped admin activity extract and custody notes for SIG/SOC2 review

Daniel / team — technical follow-up with specifics we will use for the test run. I've included inline answers where helpful.

Export schema (fields we will populate):
- utc_timestamp (ISO8601)
- actor_email / actor_id (internal id + canonical email)
- action_type (role_change, key_rotation, console_login, api_token_issue, permission_update, service_restart)
- resource_id, resource_type
- ip_address, user_agent, geo_country (derived)
- session_id, request_id, trace_id (when available)
- change_summary (short text), diff_ref (link to prior_state if > 500 bytes)
- kv_cache_ops (when operator touched in-memory caching) 

Export mechanics and security:
- Script: forensic-export.sh in internal repo (link: git.internal.redwood.com/redwood/infrastructure/export-scripts). It runs extraction against the operator-ledger snapshot and streams JSONL to S3 multipart upload with server-side encryption (SSE-KMS).
- Manifest: manifest.jsonl (human readable) + manifest.sig (Ed25519 signature by our audit service key). Manifest includes run_id, file list, SHA256 per file, sampling notes, and contact alias for the operator.
- Checksums: SHA256 (hex). We can also include a detached PGP signature if you require external verification.

PII handling:
- Our default: exclude request payloads and redact values for fields labeled sensitive (email -> email_hash, ip -> ip_trunc4). If you need raw payloads, we'll require a Data Access Agreement and additional logging controls.

Chain-of-custody notes:
- Each export run logs: who initiated (internal user id), job_id, host node id, export_start/end, artifacts written, KMS key id. Those entries are captured in the audit index and will be included in the manifest.

Staging and delivery window:
- We'll stage to an S3 bucket in us-west-2. Default presigned link lifetime 7 days (we can extend on request). Files kept in staging 30 days; after that they are auto-deleted unless you request long-term retention.

Test run plan:
- Test slice (2026-03-20 -> 2026-03-26) run on 2026-04-21 morning; Karthik will send the presigned link and manifest.
- Please confirm whether you want payload_ref expansion for the test.

Open items for Acme to confirm:
1) Accept JSONL gz + signed manifest?
2) If you need raw payloads, sign DAA?
3) Confirm presigned link lifetime (7 days default)

Thanks — will follow up with results of the 1-week extract.

— Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Audit & Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Daniel Park <dpark@acmehealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: security@acmehealth.com
Date: 2026-04-22T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: scoped admin activity extract and custody notes for SIG/SOC2 review

Jordan / Karthik — thanks for the thorough plan. A few quick confirmations before the test run:  
- JSONL gz + signed manifest is fine. Please include SHA256 in hex and manifest.sig.
- Presigned link lifetime: can you set to 7 days for the test run and we will request a 90-day staging window if the audit team needs it after review.
- PII: for the test slice keep payloads redacted (email_hash, ip_trunc4).

If you can provide the presigned link, manifest, and an S3 bucket ACL snippet (to show it's private), we'll route to legal and our SOC2 lead. Schedule a 30-minute handoff call if anything unexpected shows up in the manifest.

We'll expect the 7-day test slice link on 2026-04-21 as indicated. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Regards,
Daniel Park
Security Engineer
Acme Health
